title: Octopus Energy Commits $500M to Living Carbon for US Land Restoration — Largest Institutional Nature-Based Carbon Deal Disclosed
detail: Octopus Energy Generation committed $500 million — plus a $13 million equity stake — to Living Carbon, a US-based nature-tech company, on April 30, 2026, making it one of the largest single institutional investments in nature-based carbon removal publicly disclosed to date. The partnership aims to restore degraded US land — primarily old mine sites and worn-out farmland — through afforestation and reforestation across Appalachia and the broader eastern United States. The investment targets 50 million tonnes of CO₂ removal over 40 years. Google, Meta, and McKinsey separately announced purchases of 131,240 tonnes of carbon removal credits from Living Carbon's existing Appalachian forest projects in the same announcement. Living Carbon's approach focuses on restoring native forest on land too degraded for agriculture, combining site remediation with native species plantings verified under rigorous carbon accounting standards. The deal is significant for several reasons: it signals growing institutional appetite for long-duration nature-based carbon removal beyond short-term offset markets; it demonstrates demand from corporate buyers (Google, Meta, McKinsey) willing to pre-purchase credits from early-stage projects; and it focuses on genuinely degraded land (former mine sites) rather than existing ecosystems, reducing concerns about additionality and permanence. However, independent analysts noted that the 50 Mt over 40 years target represents approximately 1.25 Mt per year — a meaningful but modest contribution relative to Octopus Energy's overall carbon footprint and the scale of global nature-based solutions needed.

media.caption: Living Carbon secures $500M from Octopus Energy to restore degraded US land and remove 50 Mt CO₂
